name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1
route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
mechanism: A fatty-acid-modified version of the natural peptide GHK, proposed to prompt skin cells to make collagen and other matrix proteins

article.summary: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 (Pal-GHK) is a fatty-acid-modified skincare peptide marketed to boost collagen, often paired with palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7. A 2025 review found surprisingly few clinical studies.
article.takeaway: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 (Pal-GHK) is the natural peptide GHK with a fatty acid attached to help it enter skin. Natural GHK is found in blood and has been linked in lab studies to collagen production and wound repair.[^1] The palmitoyl version is widely used in anti-wrinkle products, usually paired with [palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7](/peptides/palmitoyl-tetrapeptide-7) as Matrixyl 3000, yet a 2025 review noted a surprising absence of clinical studies on it.[^2] The best human data come from multi-ingredient creams,[^3] and a 2026 skin study found the pair mostly in the outermost layer.[^4] **Evidence is limited.**
glance: Serums and eye creams, usually once or twice daily

blocks.text: GHK (glycine, histidine, lysine) is a natural peptide present in blood, saliva and urine that declines with age. In lab studies it stimulated collagen and related matrix molecules and accelerated wound repair.[^1] The same peptide bound to copper is covered in the [copper tripeptide-1](/peptides/copper-tripeptide-1) entry.

Plain GHK is water-loving and does not cross skin well. Attaching palmitic acid, a fatty acid, raises permeability, according to a 2025 review of topical GHK.[^2] The theory is that the modified peptide can reach the layers where collagen is made.

rows: Review of topical GHK and Pal-GHK (2025)
Cell studies support an anti-wrinkle role, but there is a surprising absence of clinical studies on Pal-GHK or GHK-Cu[^2]
12-week eye-cream study with Pal-GHK and Pal-GQPR (2024)
Hydration +28%, elasticity +19% and collagen density +55% on instruments, but the cream held other actives and the abstract describes no comparison group[^3]
Three volunteers, serum with both peptides (2026)
Both peptides were detected through the outer stratum corneum, with signal falling steeply with depth[^4]

blocks.text: Pal-GHK is found in serums, eye creams and moisturizers, most often alongside palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7. In the 12-week eye-cream study, improvements in wrinkles and texture were reported by week 8, but the cream contained several actives.[^3] Labels rarely state the peptide concentration.

The eye-cream study described a high safety profile for the finished product,[^3] but safety data for the peptide itself are scarce. Irritation or allergy to other ingredients in the formula is the usual risk.
Cosmetics do not need FDA approval before sale, and a product that claims to change how skin works can be treated as a drug.[^5]

Pal-GHK is a popular ingredient built on interesting biology, but its own clinical record is nearly empty. It is a reasonable add-on in a moisturizer, with modest expectations and no substitute for sunscreen.

evidence.label: Very limited: combination products, few clinical studies
evidence.text: A 2025 review describes cell support but a surprising lack of clinical studies on Pal-GHK.[^2] Human data come from multi-ingredient creams, so the peptide's own effect cannot be isolated.[^3]

faq.q: What is the difference between GHK-Cu and palmitoyl tripeptide-1?
faq.a: GHK-Cu is GHK bound to copper, while palmitoyl tripeptide-1 is GHK with a fatty acid attached. Each change affects how the molecule behaves on skin, and both have limited clinical data.[^2] See [copper tripeptide-1](/peptides/copper-tripeptide-1).

faq.q: Is it the same as Matrixyl?
faq.a: Matrixyl is a family of branded ingredients. Matrixyl 3000 pairs palmitoyl tripeptide-1 with palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7,[^4] while the original Matrixyl is [palmitoyl pentapeptide-4](/peptides/palmitoyl-pentapeptide-4).

faq.q: How long does it take to work?
faq.a: The 12-week study measured results at 4, 8 and 12 weeks, with wrinkle and texture gains reported by week 8, but with other ingredients in the cream.[^3]
